core_action_logic.name: OBSERVE
core_action_logic.description: Identify the people, place, resources and immediate problem.

core_action_logic.name: IDENTIFY
core_action_logic.description: Define the actual problem instead of reacting emotionally.

core_action_logic.name: PLAN
core_action_logic.description: Choose a workable sequence using available resources.

core_action_logic.name: INITIATE
core_action_logic.description: Take the first useful action; avoid passive waiting.

core_action_logic.name: COORDINATE
core_action_logic.description: Involve the right people and communicate clearly.

core_action_logic.name: EXECUTE
core_action_logic.description: Carry out the plan while adapting to new information.

core_action_logic.name: RESULT
core_action_logic.description: Show a realistic, measurable or observable outcome.

tat_framework_rules: Observe -> Identify -> Plan -> Initiate -> Coordinate -> Execute -> Result
Use the profession as a source of realistic action. Do not force a profession into the picture.
If a profession is relevant, use its knowledge, tools, responsibilities and work environment to create a practical response.
The OLQ labels are practice prompts, not a claim about how any individual candidate will be assessed.

questions: Does the profession actually matter to the solution?
Is the problem specific rather than vague?
Are actions practical with available resources?
Does the story include appropriate coordination?
Does the protagonist adapt when required?
Is the result realistic rather than heroic or exaggerated?
Does the story avoid unnecessary drama?
Could the same action sequence work in real life?
mistakes_to_avoid: Writing a profession description instead of a story.
Using the same generic action for every profession.
Adding unrealistic authority, resources or outcomes.
Making the protagonist solve everything alone.
Using unnecessary violence or melodrama when a practical solution is available.
Trying to display every OLQ explicitly instead of letting actions demonstrate them.
